result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A moves well from the reader's problem to what's inside to the price, and gives the US-only and not-tax-advice limits their own visible section. It never names the course 'Quiet Books', though, and it invents details about Dana: that she worked mainly for creative freelancers and 'sat across from hundreds' of clients. B uses the course name and states the disclaimers clearly, but it makes up more: Dana's agency, startup and nonprofit clients, 'hundreds of freelancers', 'audit-ready', 'saves most freelancers hours', and Q&A calls starting 'this month', plus a 'Why Now' urgency close that the fact sheet doesn't support. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B moves more clearly from the reader's money worries to what they get and then the price. It gives the 45-minute Q&A length and puts the US-only and not-tax-advice limits in a section buyers will see, but it never uses the name 'Quiet Books', invents that Dana has worked with 'hundreds of illustrators and designers', and adds a claim about LLCs and S-corps that isn't in the fact sheet. A names the course and states its limits clearly, but it also invents Dana's client history ('agencies, startups, nonprofits, and hundreds of freelancers'), plus 'audit-ready', 'saves most freelancers hours', and 'Q&A calls start this month'; it also drops the 45-minute length and reads more like a flat feature list.
